programme: NPAS2 and RORC converge on the core clock loop — both target BMAL1 directly, NPAS2 as a CLOCK-paralog bHLH-PAS partner and RORC as the ROR nuclear receptor that transactivates Bmal1 — with RORC additionally carrying a Th17/IL-17 effector programme (IL17A, IL17F, IL23R, IFNG, IL6, TNF, FOXP3, IL22, CCR6). HNF4G sits alongside as a distinct nuclear-receptor module running classic hepatocyte-identity genes (AFP, CYP2D6, HNF1A, AGT, SHBG, GHR).
role_in_a: In COPD, RORC's Th17 output (IL17A/IL17F/IL23R/IFNG/IL6/TNF) is directly documented as part of immune dysregulation and airway inflammation signatures; NPAS2's convergence with RORC on BMAL1 places this in the peripheral circadian-immune axis increasingly implicated in COPD exacerbation biology, though that link is not itself documented in the retrieved record.
role_in_b: In liver cancer, HNF4G's target set is the canonical HNF4-family hepatocyte-differentiation programme; loss of this programme is a textbook route to hepatocellular dedifferentiation and malignant transformation, but nothing in the retrieved record (no Open Targets association, no papers) places HNF4G in liver cancer specifically — this role is inferred from the gene family's general biology, not from evidence in hand.
shared_axis: If real, the shared axis would be a nuclear-receptor/clock-output network in which circadian control of immune effector output (RORC/NPAS2, relevant to lung mucosal Th17 tone) and circadian control of hepatocyte metabolic/differentiation state (HNF4G) are two tissue-specific readouts of the same clock machinery, explaining why clock-adjacent nuclear receptors would recur in both an inflammatory airway disease and a metabolic organ cancer.
reasoning: The RORC-NPAS2 pairing is internally coherent (shared BMAL1 target, documented RORC role in COPD immune dysregulation), but HNF4G — the only factor with a plausible liver-cancer role — has zero placement in either disease in the retrieved record, and no paper here connects COPD and liver cancer through this axis at all. Two of the three carrying factors have no retrieved literature signal, and none of the twelve listed factors clears even half of the 130 comparisons (top is 61/130), so the recurrence itself is modest, not the '26/28'-type strong signal the framework calls out.
support: PMID 42196213 — places RORC in COPD via a three-gene immune-dysregulation signature; PMID 37650285 — places RORC in COPD via circRNA-ceRNA networks in peripheral blood; PMID 38786101 — places RORC in COPD via reduced PD-L1+ dendritic cell populations. none found for NPAS2 or HNF4G in either disease, and none found connecting COPD and liver cancer through this axis.
how_to_falsify: Run ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq for NPAS2 and RORC in COPD airway epithelium to test whether they actually co-occupy the BMAL1 locus in that tissue; in parallel, profile HNF4G occupancy at AFP/CYP2D6/HNF1A in matched HCC tumor vs adjacent normal liver. If NPAS2 and RORC do not co-bind BMAL1 in airway cells, or HNF4G occupancy at hepatocyte-identity genes is unchanged in tumor tissue, the proposed shared axis fails.
caveats: The 130 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so most of the 130 are clinical-subgroup splits within the same two cohorts, not independent replications — the recurrence counts should be read as pseudo-replicated, not as 130 separate validations. All concordant factors here sit in a narrow 41-47% band, well short of near-universal recurrence. FOXA2 — the more obvious lung/liver dual-identity transcription factor — is excluded as single-view (it topped one patient group at 0.991 with only 16% overall recurrence) and is deliberately not used to build this account. Liver-cancer literature coverage for every factor in this list is described as particularly thin, so the absence of liver-cancer citations reflects a retrieval gap, not a confirmed absence of connection.
